final_message:
The bug is fixed, and your reproduction test now passes along with the rest of the suite (25 tests).

**Root cause:** `record_failure` in `billing/dunning.py` had an off-by-one in the retry check. It used `attempt_count < len(offsets)`, but `retry_offsets_days` lists retries *after* the first attempt. With `[1]`, the first failed charge at subscribe time was already treated as the last one. The final action ran straight away on a subscription that was still `active`, and `active → unpaid` isn't an allowed transition. That's the `InvalidStateError` you saw.

**Fix:** I changed the check to `<=`. The first failure now schedules the retry and moves the subscription to `past_due`. After the immediate cancel, the retry on day 1 fails with the subscription `canceled`, so the invoice is marked `uncollectible`.

I wrote `answer.json` as `{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}`.

My first attempt was a different fix, which forced a `past_due` step before the final action. It cleared the error but left the invoice `open`, so I reverted it.

I used your test only as a temporary file and removed it afterwards, so it isn't in the suite. Say so if you want it added permanently.

steps.command: cd billing && cat dunning.py; sed -n 20,60p subscriptions.py; sed -n 130,155p subscriptions.py
sed -n 20,50p engine.py; grep -n "def cancel" -B3 -A15 engine.py | head -5

cd .. && python - <<'E'
p='billing/dunning.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''    action = policy["final_action"]
''','''    if subscription["status"] in ("active", "trialing"):
        transition(ctx, subscription, "past_due")
    action = policy["final_action"]
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
cat >> tests/test_dunning_extra.py <<'E'
E
rm tests/test_dunning_extra.py
cat > /tmp/t.py <<'E'
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cat > tests/test_tmp_repro.py <<'E'
def test_retries_exhausted_after_cancel_marks_uncollectible():
    from conftest import World

    w = World({"retry_offsets_days": [1], "final_action": "mark_unpaid"})
    cus = w.customer(last4="0002")
    sub = w.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(w.monthly["id"], 1)])
    w.engine.cancel(sub["id"], at_period_end=False)
    w.advance_days(1)
    [inv] = w.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert sub["status"] == "canceled"
    assert inv["status"] == "uncollectible"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_tmp_repro.py 2>&1 | tail -15
git checkout billing/dunning.py && cat billing/payments.py | head -80; grep -n "def advance_days" -A12 tests/conftest.py; grep -n "def subscribe" -A25 billing/engine.py

sed -i 's/if invoice\["attempt_count"\] < len(offsets):/if invoice["attempt_count"] <= len(offsets):/' billing/dunning.py
echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8; rm tests/test_tmp_repro.py; git status --short

cat > tests/test_tmp_repro.py <<'E'
def test_retries_exhausted_after_cancel_marks_uncollectible():
    from conftest import World

    w = World({"retry_offsets_days": [1], "final_action": "mark_unpaid"})
    cus = w.customer(last4="0002")
    sub = w.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(w.monthly["id"], 1)])
    w.engine.cancel(sub["id"], at_period_end=False)
    w.advance_days(1)
    [inv] = w.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert sub["status"] == "canceled"
    assert inv["status"] == "uncollectible"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -8; rm tests/test_tmp_repro.py; git status --short; git diff; cat answer.json
